[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Modern Data Stack & Cloud DW Architecture"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Introduction to the Modern Data Stack (MDS)"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Modern Data Stack (MDS) represents a paradigm shift from traditional, monolithic on-premise data warehousing (like traditional Teradata or Oracle setups) to a decoupled, cloud-native ecosystem. In an MDS, each component of the data pipeline is handled by best-in-class specialized SaaS tools: ingestion (e.g., Fivetran, Airbyte), storage and compute (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), transformation (e.g., dbt), and orchestration (e.g., Apache Airflow, Dagster)."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Core Architecture Patterns"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike the traditional Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) architecture where transformations occurred before loading into the warehouse, the MDS heavily favors Extract, Load, Transform (ELT). Raw data is loaded directly into the cloud data warehouse first, preserving lineage and allowing compute power of the cloud to handle heavy data transformations."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Storage-Compute Separation: Modern cloud data warehouses decouple storage (cloud object stores like AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage) from compute (elastic virtual warehouses). This allows independent scaling and cost optimization."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Analytics Engineering: Tools like dbt (data build tool) introduce software engineering best practices--such as modularity, version control, automated testing, and CI/CD--directly into SQL-based transformations."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementation Example using dbt and SQL"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of a modern dbt staging model that cleans up raw customer data extracted from an operational database. This model casts data types, standardizes naming conventions, and handles basic null checks."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"with source_data as (
    select
        id as customer_id,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        email,
        updated_at
    from {{ source('operational_db', 'raw_customers') }}
),

cleaned as (
    select
        customer_id,
        initcap(trim(first_name)) as first_name,
        initcap(trim(last_name)) as last_name,
        lower(trim(email)) as email,
        updated_at
    -- Exclude test records
    where email not like '%test.com'
)

select * from cleaned"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Best Practices for Cloud DW Governance"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Implement principle of least privilege using granular permissions on schemas, tables, and views."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cost Management: Set up automated warehouse auto-suspension policies, query timeout limits, and resource monitors to prevent runaway cloud bills."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Quality Testing: Write schema tests (such as unique, not_null, accepted_values) inside your transformation layer to catch anomalies before analytics reports are generated."}]
